newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Death toll seen rising in Sri Lanka rebel attack.
newsitem.headline: Death toll seen rising in Sri Lanka rebel attack.

text.p: Sri Lankan security forces were consolidating their position on Friday in a key northern town after repulsing a Tamil rebel attack in which more than 500 guerrillas died or were wounded, military officials said.
"Forces are mopping up the last of the resistance," an army official in Colombo told Reuters.
The bodies of 60 government soldiers had been recovered as of Thursday night, the Ministry of Defence said.
Officials said the toll was likely to rise during Friday as scores of badly wounded soldiers were flown from the battlefront to hospitals in the capital Colombo.

The rebels' official Voice of Tigers radio broadcast on Friday said hundreds of government soldiers had been killed when the rebels used human-wave tactics and suicide bombers to overrun defences at Paranthan, a junction town 280 km (185 miles) north of Colombo.
Paranthan is the first military base to be attacked by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).this year.
The defence ministry said on Thursday that security forces reinforced by aircraft and troops had killed or wounded more than 500 rebels and successfully repulsed the attack.
It said 232 soldiers had been wounded in the pre-dawn attack carried out by the LTTE.
A London-based spokesmen for the LTTE on Thursday denied the army statement of 500 rebel casualties.
"The government claim is totally false," LTTE spokesman Anton Raja said by telephone. "It routinely exaggerates the LTTE deaths to maintain flagging morale among supporters and troops."
Military spokesman Brigadier Tissa Jayatunga said on Friday that soldiers had destroyed several pieces of artillery to prevent them falling into rebel hands but declined to say how many.

The LTTE, which is fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in this predominantly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island, were driven out of their Jaffna peninsula stronghold by government forces in April last year.
In July last year, the rebels overran a key army base at northeastern Mullaitivu, killing or capturing more than 1,000 men, dealing the military its biggest blow in the war, now in its 14th year.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war. The LTTE says the toll is much higher.
